title: Why Interest Rates Matter
subtitle: Borrowing, valuation and expectations
rightsNote: Original educational text; accompanying audio is synthetic demo audio, NOT a VOA recording.

lines.english: When a central bank raises interest rates, borrowing usually becomes more expensive.
lines.chinese: 当中央银行提高利率时，借贷通常会变得更加昂贵。

lines.english: Businesses may postpone investment projects, while households may reduce spending.
lines.chinese: 企业可能推迟投资项目，家庭则可能减少支出。

lines.english: Higher interest rates can also change the way investors value companies.
lines.chinese: 更高的利率也可能改变投资者对企业的估值方式。

lines.english: Analysts often discount future cash flows to estimate what a business is worth today.
lines.chinese: 分析师通常对未来现金流进行折现，以估计企业今天的价值。

lines.english: When the discount rate rises, distant cash flows generally become less valuable in today's terms.
lines.chinese: 当折现率上升时，较远期的现金流以现值计算通常会下降。

lines.english: This is one reason why fast-growing companies can be sensitive to interest rate changes.
lines.chinese: 这也是高速成长型公司可能对利率变化较为敏感的原因之一。

lines.english: However, stock prices also depend on profits, competition, risk and market expectations.
lines.chinese: 不过，股价还取决于利润、竞争、风险和市场预期。

lines.english: A thoughtful investor asks not only what changed, but also what the market had already expected.
lines.chinese: 审慎的投资者不仅关心发生了什么变化，也关心市场此前已经预期了什么。
